newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria to talk to Paris Club lenders one by one.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria to talk to Paris Club lenders one by one.

text.p: Nigeria plans to talk to bilateral Paris Club creditors one by one outside the usual joint framework to renegotiate ballooning external debt, finance ministry officials said on Tuesday.

One finance ministry official said a delegation would leave Nigeria on Wednesday on a two-week debt negotiation mission beginning in London. The team includes officials from the finance ministry, central bank and National Planning Commission.
"The debt talks with the Paris are going to be on a parallel basis, that is to individual countries as against the usually collective manner," said the official.
The delegation leaving Abuja on Wednesday will visit London, Brussels and New York.
A central bank official said "The delegation is going for the normal annual meeting with the country's creditors and they are also to try to ascertain the actual amount Nigeria owes.'
Nigeria estimates its foreign debt as at the end of 1996 at about $28 billion and more than two thirds of it is to the Paris Club of Western government creditors.
Experts say the debt stock is much higher if arrears of interests that have fallen due but not repaid are added.
The military government in Abuja has not bothered to service the Paris Club debts while it regularly services the debts it owes to the London Club of Western creditor banks.

The government says it wants the Paris Club to reschedule the official debts but this is not possible until the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund can approve Nigeria's medium term economic programme.

Approving the programme at the moment seems unlikely because of lack of privatisation of loss-making but potentially profitable state enterprises and a dual exchange rate which makes Nigerian government accounting less transparent than required by the Bretton Woods institutions.

The stalemate has left Nigeria's debt crisis hanging and finance minister Anthony Ani reiterated at a workshop in Abuja on Monday that Nigeria will retain its policy not to contract any new foreign debt.
"It is in order to ameliorate the problem of debt that government has for the time being placed an embargo on new external loans until the debt crisis is brought under firm control," Ani said.
